title: Open-label phase I/II clinical trial of SARS-CoV-2 receptor binding domain-tetanus toxoid conjugate vaccine (FINLAY-FR-2) in combination with receptor binding domain-protein vaccine (FINLAY-FR-1A) in children.
ehr_evidence: A phase I/II open-label, adaptive, and multicenter clinical trial that collected data through physical examination, parent interview, and phase I clinical laboratory assays (PCR SARS-CoV-2, serum sampling, ELISA, neutralization titers, and T-cell responses), not pre-existing electronic health records.
summary: A phase I/II open-label, adaptive, multicenter clinical trial evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of a heterologous two-dose FINLAY-FR-2 (SOBERANA 02) plus third-dose FINLAY-FR-1A (SOBERANA Plus) SARS-CoV-2 RBD vaccine scheme in 350 children 3-18 years old in Havana, Cuba.
key_findings: Local pain was the most common adverse event (47.7%); no serious or severe vaccine-associated adverse events occurred (serious AE 0.3%, severe AE 0.0%).
Two doses of FINLAY-FR-2 induced seroconversion in 96.2% of participants (95% CI 93.5; 98.0) and satisfied the trial hypothesis (>50% with lower 95% CI boundary >0.3).
The heterologous third dose with FINLAY-FR-1A increased seroconversion to 100% and anti-RBD IgG to 325.7 UA/ml (25th-75th percentile 141.5; 613.8), P < 0.005.
Geometric mean neutralizing titers were 173.8 (95% CI 131.7; 229.5) vs Alpha, 142 (95% CI 101.3; 198.9) vs Delta, 24.8 (95% CI 16.8; 36.6) vs Beta, and 99.2 (95% CI 67.8; 145.4) vs Omicron.
IFN-γ- and IL-4-secreting cells were statistically higher (P < 0.001) than baseline levels.
Non-inferiority was met versus 19-39 y/o young adults, with cVNT50 GMT ratio 1.25 (95% CI 0.77; 2.02) for children 3-18 y/o.
Predicted clinical efficacy was 91.3% (95% CI 84.6; 95.1) after two doses and 97.4% (95% CI 91.5; 99.2) after three doses vs the D614G variant.
captured_features: Adverse events (local and systemic, solicited and unsolicited)
Anti-RBD IgG seroconversion rate and titers
mVNT50 and cVNT50 neutralizing titers against variants
Demographic variables (age, sex, skin color, weight, height, BMI)
study_design: Phase I/II open-label, adaptive, multicenter clinical trial (no placebo control group)
population: 350 children and adolescents 3-18 years old (mean 11.3 years) recruited from the community primary health system in Havana, Cuba
exposure_domain: SARS-CoV-2 RBD vaccine (FINLAY-FR-2/SOBERANA 02 conjugate plus FINLAY-FR-1A/SOBERANA Plus heterologous third dose)
limitations: No placebo-controlled group due to ethical concerns during the Delta wave, the main design limitation.
Immunobridging comparison used no concurrent reference population (young adults vaccinated in prior trials).
Clinical efficacy was predicted from immunological surrogates rather than measured directly.
